title: Ottoman warships were dragged over a hill to besiege Constantinople
body: The defenders of Constantinople had stretched a great chain, floating on logs, across the mouth of the Golden Horn, and no Ottoman ship could force it. So the 21-year-old sultan Mehmed II had a road of greased logs laid across Galata, the hill on the inlet’s north side. On **22 April 1453** his ships were hauled overland and slid into the harbour behind the chain, and the outnumbered defenders suddenly had another long stretch of wall to guard. The city fell on 29 May, after a siege of 53 days, and with it the Byzantine Empire.

slides.alt: Sketch map: the triangular city of Constantinople, the Golden Horn inlet to its north closed by a chain at its mouth, Galata on the far shore, and a dashed arrow showing ships hauled over the hill from the Bosporus into the inlet.
slides.caption: The defenders’ chain closed the mouth of the Golden Horn harbour, so the Ottoman fleet went round it: over the hill behind Galata.

left.label: Ottomans
left.text: Some 50,000 to 80,000 soldiers by modern estimates, a fleet, and the cannon-maker Orban’s 8.2-metre bombard, dragged from Edirne by 60 oxen.

right.label: Defenders
right.text: About 7,000 men, 2,000 of them foreigners, spread along the city’s walls.

slides.heading: Besiegers and defenders, by numbers
slides.note: About 7,000 defenders faced 50,000 to 80,000 Ottomans by modern estimates; the circles use 50,000.

events.text: Ships are hauled over the hill into the Golden Horn
The walls are breached and the city falls

slides.heading: Why go over land?
slides.text: The chain was meant to keep the inlet safe, so the sea walls along the Golden Horn were thinly held. Once Ottoman vessels were floating inside it, the defenders were forced to send part of their small force to guard those walls too.

slides.question: How long did the siege of Constantinople last in 1453?
slides.explanation: From 6 April to 29 May 1453: 53 days, with the ships crossing the hill on 22 April, roughly halfway through.

slides.heading: Which one is not at Constantinople?
slides.explanation: Galata is the hill across the inlet, the Golden Horn the inlet itself and the Bosporus the strait beside the city. Edirne is the city the great bombard was dragged from.
